question: When two-way traffic must share one lane for a limited distance, what coordination rule and control methods apply?
model_answer: Direct Answer: When traffic in both directions must use a single lane for a limited distance, movements from each end of the section must be coordinated, except in the limited self-regulating case. Permitted control methods include flagger control (one or two flaggers), temporary traffic control signals, and — on short, low-volume worksites with full mutual visibility — self-regulation. Where two-way traffic operates on one roadway of a normally-divided highway, opposing traffic must be physically separated; markings and signing alone are prohibited. Standards (mandatory): - "Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, when traffic in both directions must use a single lane for a limited distance, movements from each end shall be coordinated." - "When two-lane, two-way traffic control must be maintained on one roadway of a normally-divided highway, opposing vehicular traffic shall be separated with either temporary traffic barriers (concrete safety-shape or approved alternate), channelizing devices, Narrow Two-Way Traffic (W6-4) signs on flexible supports (see Section 6H.17), or a temporary raised island throughout the length of the two-way operation. The use of markings and complementary signing, by themselves, shall not be used." Options (permitted): - When the one-lane, two-way TTC zone is short enough for a flagger to see from one end to the other, traffic may be controlled by either a single flagger or by a flagger at each end of the section. - On a low-volume street or road with a short work space, where road users from both directions can see traffic approaching from the opposite direction through and beyond the worksite, movement through the constriction may be self-regulating. - Traffic control signals may be used to control vehicular traffic movements in one-lane, two-way TTC zones. Citations: - Section 6E.01 Standard §1 (p.787) - Section 6N.14 Standard §2 (p.850) - Section 6E.02 Option §2 (p.787) - Section 6E.01 Option §4 (p.787) - Section 6E.05 Option §1 (p.788) - Section 6N.09 Support §6 (p.846)
gold_answer: Movements from both ends must be coordinated, except for a short, low-volume, mutually visible work zone that can self-regulate. Methods include flaggers, flag transfer, a pilot car, temporary traffic signals, or stop/yield control.
